purpose: Crisaborole is a skin ointment used to treat mild to moderate eczema (also called atopic dermatitis) in adults and children as young as 3 months old. It helps calm red, itchy, and irritated skin caused by eczema. It is a non-steroidal option, meaning it does not contain cortisone or steroids.
how_it_works: Eczema causes your immune system to overreact and create inflammation in your skin. Crisaborole works by blocking an enzyme called PDE-4 that contributes to that inflammation. By blocking this enzyme, the ointment helps reduce the redness, itching, and irritation in your skin.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is a burning or stinging feeling right where you apply it, especially when you first start using it. This usually gets better over time. Some people may also notice mild skin irritation at the application site.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have any allergies, especially to crisaborole or any ingredients in the product. Avoid getting the ointment in your eyes, mouth, or nose. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before using this medication. If your skin gets worse or you develop a severe reaction such as hives or difficulty breathing, stop using it and seek medical help right away.
typical_dosing: Apply a thin layer of the ointment to the affected skin areas twice a day (morning and evening). Use it only on the areas of skin your doctor told you to treat. Wash your hands after applying unless your hands are the area being treated.
